expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: The structural case in item 0 is sound and sourced (80-week double-blind from a 2025-03-26 enrolment completion, registry primary completion 2026-10, baseline-only CTAD posters, a 2026-10-22 restatement of 'late 2026') so the print cannot carry the only thing this stock trades on, but the step from that to a disappointed 20% unwind is inference and not a document, and the company already deflated the hope four days before the print; item 1's cash walk is arithmetic anyone can do and the hunter itself calls it mostly priced, so it is a small negative that only bites if the 10-Q shows ATM use at ~$2; the big abs_move is the $2 price and 80% realised vol, not conviction, and p_up carries the uncertainty.

opus55.note: A 20% run-up into a print that almost certainly reiterates 'late 2026' topline (item 0), plus a repeat going-concern 10-Q on a shrinking cash pile (item 1), gives a mild downside lean on a volatile microcap; the topline itself is outside the window.

sonnet55.note: Item 0: the 20% run-up into an early report date, with ALTITUDE-AD topline most likely in December, makes a bare reiteration the base case. This is inference only, the bar is disputed and there is no option anchor, so it is a small negative.

fable51.note: Rests on item 0: a 20% five-session run-up into a date notice when the registry (primary completion 2026-10, estimated) and the company's own 2026-10-22 release make the print a bare 'late 2026' reiteration, with item 1's going-concern/possible ATM use a small priced negative; the sign is inference so p_up stays near 50, while 80% realised vol on a $2 biotech sets abs_move well above the 3.0% median.

opus5.note: Rests on item 1 against item 0: the CEO pre-committed on 2026-09-09, two-thirds through the quarter, to the first positive phone net accounts in three years and the top end of the 750k-1M guide, and subscriber delivery has been bought at all seven prints under him (+11.8, +5.8, +1.6), while AT&T's light 379k adds on flat churn arguably point the switchers toward VZ rather than away; against that, the same tape sold AT&T's beat-and-raise on 10-21 and VZ already paid 3.2% of sympathy for it, the -4.67 skew means my positive lean agrees with what the option market has already paid for, and the baseline's event-implied move is 0.0 after netting elevated realised vol — so near-neutral with a slight tilt up, and the satellite derating is priced at -10% with the rebuttal two-sided.

opus55.note: The CEO's late-quarter commitment to positive phone net accounts and top-end net adds (item 1), set against a bar lowered by the SpaceX derating (item 2), outweighs the AT&T beat being sold (item 0); a modest upside lean that agrees with the call-bid skew and so is partly priced.

sonnet55.note: The CEO's late-quarter commitment to positive phone net adds (item 1), the call-bid skew and seven straight positive prints lean up. AT&T's sold beat-and-raise and the Starlink overhang offset most of it, and none of it is a number the market has not seen.

fable51.note: Rests on item 1 (CEO's late-quarter top-end net-add commitment on a name whose last seven prints all reacted up, with Q3 2025's 44k an easy comp) and item 2 (a bar lowered 10% by the SpaceX deal, call-bid skew at -4.67), against item 0, where the tape sold AT&T's beat-and-raise; net-add consensus is unsourced and the relief is partly in the 7% bounce, so a mild lean at a 4% scale between the 2.26% median and the recent 5.8%/11.8% prints.

opus5.note: A wash of same-region peer read-throughs that landed after BFST last spoke — Investar's +6bp NIM beat is the most direct comp and is positive, Home Bancorp's credit miss is idiosyncratic and runs against BFST's own falling-NPA document trend, and the post-hike deposit-cost turn at HWC/Third Coast is the best-evidenced negative but is contradicted by Investar and unquantifiable because the 10-Q rate-sensitivity table could not be read; the one genuinely unaggregated primary document is item 4, the Chief Banking Officer's quiet 5.02 resignation with no successor named into a guide that depends on high-single-digit loan growth, which I size as a real but print-day-modest negative; net a small lean down on a name at its 52-week high with all-Buy coverage and insiders out at this price.

opus55.note: Peer proxies offset: Investar's NIM gain (item 0) against post-hike deposit-cost pressure (item 2), the CBO departure on the loan-growth engine (item 4) and a Home Bancorp credit read (item 1), on a stock at its 52-week high; a slight negative lean only.

sonnet55.note: The Investar NIM read-through and the guided ROA path (items 0 and 3) offset Home Bancorp credit, deposit-cost and executive-departure items. All are proxies or partly priced, so the net is a near-zero lean.

fable51.note: Rests on items 2 and 4 against item 0: regional deposit costs turning up after the September hike (HWC, TCBX primary releases) and the quiet 5.02 departure of the Chief Banking Officer with no successor, on a name 1% off its high with all-Buy coverage and a building short, partly offset by Investar's NIM read-through; all proxies or partly priced, so a modest lean at the 3.85% median scale.
